title: Christ and Marriage
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ and marriage teaches that marriage points beyond itself to the faithful, sacrificial love of Christ for His people. Marriage is not ultimate, but it is designed to reflect covenant love, holiness, and devotion under God.
summary: Christ and marriage teaches that marriage points beyond itself to the faithful, sacrificial love of Christ for His people. Marriage is not ultimate, but it is designed to reflect covenant love, holiness, and devotion under God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the true Bridegroom who loves, cleanses, keeps, and prepares His people for Himself. Earthly marriage finds its highest meaning when it reflects His faithful love for the church.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture uses marriage language to reveal covenant faithfulness. God’s love for His people is described with deep commitment, jealousy for holiness, and promise-keeping love.

Ephesians teaches that marriage points to Christ and the church. This mystery gives marriage a meaning deeper than romance, convenience, or social arrangement.

Christ’s love is sacrificial and sanctifying. He gave Himself for the church, cleanses her, and prepares her in holiness. This pattern corrects selfish, harsh, or shallow views of marriage.

Marriage is temporary, but the reality it points to is eternal. The marriage supper of the Lamb shows the final joy of Christ with His redeemed people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
This doctrine protects marriage from being reduced to personal happiness or cultural tradition. Marriage is meant to display something holy, faithful, and Gospel-shaped.

It also comforts those who are unmarried, widowed, abandoned, or wounded. The ultimate hope is not earthly marriage, but belonging to Christ, the faithful Bridegroom who never forsakes His people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let Christ define the meaning of marriage. If you are married, seek to reflect His faithful and sacrificial love. If you are not married, do not believe you are missing your highest identity; your deepest belonging is in Christ and His eternal kingdom.
